threads.name: Daśaratha's word to Viśvāmitra

opened.what: The king assures the sage he will do whatever is asked, before hearing it.

tested.what: He offers the army and himself instead.

threads.why: The engine of the entire arc. Six films of a man trying not to pay what he already owes.

threads.name: The two boons owed to Kaikeyī

opened.what: She saved him in a battle; he granted two boons, unnamed and unspent.
opened.note: Referred to, not narrated, at the point we enter.

closed.what: She names them: Bharata crowned, Rāma exiled fourteen years.

threads.why: The longest unpaid debt in the first two books, and the one that destroys the man who granted it. He is generous in Bāla and it kills him in Ayodhyā.
threads.echo_note: THE central rhyme of the first two kāṇḍas. Twice a man gives his word without counting, and twice it takes his son. Arc 7 is the rehearsal; Ayodhyā is the performance.

threads.name: Rāvaṇa's boon from Brahmā

opened.what: Granted invulnerability to gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas and rākṣasas.

threads.why: The longest arc in the epic and its central irony. His contempt for humans is the hole in his armour, written into the boon at the moment of asking.
threads.staging_note: In M4 the boon is stated as a plain fact in a big room. The irony is never pointed at. It pays off five kāṇḍas later.

threads.name: The sage's observance

opened.what: Under the rite, he may not release his anger or utter a curse.

threads.why: Recorded precisely because it is NOT a mystery. The source answers it where it raises it. Staging it as a withheld secret would be an invention, and this node exists to stop that.

threads.name: Agastya's curse on Tāṭakā

opened.what: After Sunda's death she attacks Agastya; he curses her to a devouring, misshapen form.

threads.why: She is not born monstrous. She is made so by a curse, in grief, after her husband is killed. This is the single most important fact for her memo — the text supplies a reason for her state and a killing that follows from it.

threads.name: Agastya's curse on Mārīca
threads.why: He is driven off in Bāla and comes back in Araṇya to be the instrument of the abduction. The man who survives film 10 is the reason Sītā is taken.

threads.name: Gautama's curse on Ahalyā

opened.what: Her husband curses her after Indra's deception.

closed.what: Released when Rāma comes to the hermitage.

threads.why: The first thing Rāma does on the road after killing is to release someone. The placement is the meaning.

threads.name: The blind parents' curse on Daśaratha

opened.what: He kills a boy by mistake, hunting by sound at a river. The boy's blind parents curse him to die as they will — grieving for a son.
opened.note: Told by Daśaratha himself, in Ayodhyā, as he is dying.

closed.what: He dies of grief for Rāma.

threads.why: The deepest irony in the first two books. Everything he does to keep his son — the refusals in arc 7, the boons in Ayodhyā — runs toward a death that was fixed before Rāma was born.
threads.staging_note: NEVER foreshadowed in Bāla. He does not know. Neither should the audience until he tells it.

threads.name: Rāma's promise to the forest sages

opened.what: He promises to rid the forest of rākṣasas.

consequence.what: Śūrpaṇakhā, Khara, and everything that follows.

threads.why: A promise made out of decency that brings the war. Rhymes with Bāla: a good man's word, and what it costs.

threads.name: The alliance by fire

opened.what: Rāma and Sugrīva swear friendship before fire. Each owes the other a killing.

threads.why: The only contract in the epic between equals, and the most argued-about act in it.

threads.name: Vālin's boon

opened.what: Half the strength of any opponent who faces him passes to him.

closed.what: Rāma shoots him from concealment — and is challenged for it by the dying man.

threads.why: The boon is the reason for the manner of the killing, and the manner is why it is still argued about.

threads.name: Kumbhakarṇa's misspoken boon

opened.what: Asking for indra-āsana he says nidrā-āsana — and is granted endless sleep.

closed.what: Woken for a war he tells his brother is wrong, and fights anyway.

threads.why: A boon ruined by a slip of the tongue. The comedy of it makes his loyalty in the war unbearable.

threads.name: The curse that protects Sītā

opened.what: Rāvaṇa is cursed that his head will split if he forces a woman who does not want him.

operates.what: It is why Sītā, held a year in the aśoka grove, is not touched.

threads.why: The single most consequential curse in the epic, narrated LAST. It explains the whole of Sundara retroactively.
threads.staging_note: Told in Uttara but operating from Araṇya onward. A structural problem and an opportunity: the Ask can answer 'why does he not force her' long before the film that explains it.

threads.name: Jaṭāyu's friendship with Daśaratha

opened.what: An old friendship between the vulture king and Rāma's father.

closed.what: He fights Rāvaṇa's chariot for a friend's son's wife, and dies of it.

threads.why: An old bird keeps a debt to a dead man. Rāma performs his funeral rites — the rites he could not perform for his own father.

threads.name: The ring

opened.what: Rāma gives Hanumān his ring as a token.

closed.what: Hanumān drops it before Sītā in the aśoka grove.

threads.why: The smallest object in the epic carrying the most. Lock it with Daśaratha's ring — same object family, one decision.

threads.name: The sandals on the throne

opened.what: Bharata takes Rāma's sandals and rules from outside the city with them on the throne.

closed.what: Rāma returns and takes them back.

threads.why: Wood on a throne for fourteen years. The most powerful object in the epic and it does nothing.

threads.name: Who Viśvāmitra was

opened.what: A sage of terrifying authority asks a king for his child, and we are told nothing of him.

closed.what: Śatānanda tells Rāma his whole history — a king who became a brahmarṣi.

threads.why: The longest withheld answer inside Bāla, and the reason the arc map exists. Editorial: the source does not frame it as a question; we do, and say so.
